name: food inflation and beef supply chain

evidence.title: Food inflation remains elevated
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Food inflation remains elevated and retail beef prices are firm.

evidence.title: Processor input-cost pressure
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Meat processors report that cattle input costs are compressing processor margins despite firm beef demand.

evidence.title: Herd rebuilding remains slow
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Cattle producers are rebuilding herds slowly because feed costs and biological capacity limit supply response.

evidence.title: Beef distribution remains tight
evidence.bounded_excerpt: Distributors report firm retailer orders for beef while processor supply remains constrained.

pattern.label: Beef supply constraint
pattern.definition: Slow cattle supply response is transmitting feed and livestock scarcity through processors and distributors into firm retail beef economics.
pattern.what_changed: Independent evidence now links slow herd rebuilding with processor input pressure and firm downstream orders.

edges.mechanism: Feed costs raise the cost of rebuilding cattle supply.
break_conditions: Feed costs ease while herd rebuilding accelerates

edges.mechanism: Cattle supply is the principal livestock input for meat processors.
break_conditions: Processors substitute away from cattle input

edges.mechanism: Processors may pass constrained beef volume into distribution channels.
Distributor availability may shape retailer beef supply and pricing.
break_conditions: Retailers source sufficient beef through other channels

rationale.revenue_exposure: Processors derive revenue from beef volume.
rationale.pricing_power: Firm demand may permit some cost pass-through.
rationale.margin_sensitivity: The filing evidence reports input-cost margin pressure.
rationale.capacity_lead_time: Biological production limits make supply response slow.
rationale.evidence_strength: Several independent sources support the chain, but distributor economics remain incomplete.

counterevidence.statement: Firm retail pricing may reflect downstream markups rather than producer scarcity alone.
counterevidence.rationale: The available evidence does not decompose margins across each intermediary.

counterevidence.statement: High cattle input costs can compress processor margins even when retail beef prices are firm.
counterevidence.rationale: Scarcity need not accrue to processors.

data_requests.subject: Distributor beef purchase contracts
data_requests.reason: This is the weakest unsupported edge between processors and retailers.

invalidation_conditions: Cattle supply expands while retail beef pricing weakens
strengthening_observations: Processor backlogs remain firm while herd rebuilding stays slow

what_changed.text: Independent evidence now links slow herd rebuilding with processor input pressure and firm distributor orders.

why_it_matters.text: A persistent cattle constraint can transmit uneven economics across producers, processors, distributors and retailers.

deliverable.transmission_text: Feed costs constrain cattle supply; cattle scarcity pressures processors; downstream transmission remains partly hypothetical.

potential_capture.text: Firm demand supports revenue, but cattle input pressure makes margin capture uncertain.

evidence_for.text: Herd rebuilding remains slow because feed costs and biological capacity constrain supply.

evidence_against.text: Processor margins are being compressed by cattle input costs.
